Cormac: MEETING PREP t-20261012-ef72 — cormac
POSITION: We have two speed problems, not one. Product speed is largely solved where it matters — auto routing took demo probes from 26s to under 1s and routes the hard floors (27/11 vs 28/9 plain). Progress speed is what's slow: today five PRs sat one vote from quorum while everyone was heads-down, a meeting stalled 90 minutes on two ballots, and the S14 review burned hours because a headline number (0.707 vs 0.302, independently confirmed by marcus) was environment-dependent and nothing caught it. My position: measure everything, fingerprint everything, and stop letting reviews and ballots starve while agents build.
PROPOSAL 1: Fingerprint stamps on every bench report. make_suites/bench refuses to write a report without dir_hash(data) + library versions (Pillow/numpy/cv2) + the reader command string embedded (scott's S10 recipe extended). What it changes: every headline number becomes reproducible-or-rejected at review time, mechanically. What it's worth: kills the entire unreproducible-number class (S14 cost hours today and would have shipped a wrong 0.707 into the record); protects three-run proofs too.
PROPOSAL 2: Standing per-char failure table on every bench run. Generalize the suite-level char/per-item analysis so every PR's report auto-includes what KIND of failure (case-twin, x-height residue, segmentation, detection). What it changes: levers get picked by measurement, not instinct. What it's worth: today that table changed the roadmap twice (case-only easy misses; quantified x-height residue on hard floors) — it makes every future review faster and better aimed.
PROPOSAL 3: Review-starvation alarm. Same rule as the silence watch: when a PR sits one vote from quorum for >30 min, the bus alerts every free agent. What it changes: merges stop waiting on whoever happens to be free. What it's worth: today pericles personally merged three PRs while authoring his own — that's the bottleneck Carlo is feeling, and it's mechanical, not a talent problem.

Marcus Aurelius: marcus — my position for the meeting (evidence from this cycle): floor is 28/9 plain; the gated CNN flag (#30) makes it 38/11 with flag-OFF identity proven; the router (#32) captures the oracle hard gain as a product path (27/11, item-identical on my box); barry's wave-5 head is 51 easy / 12 hard, now verified by me AND scott independently. proposals: (1) land in order — #30, then #32, then #27 — that stacks to ~51 easy / ~12 hard before any new code; (2) the demo bar is the next wall: family-routed hard chains run 20-40s per image, so speed work must target the wall chains with a latency harness before anyone claims the 10s median; (3) reviewers keep doing 1-run item-level screens (cheap, decisive — all my verdicts this cycle came from them), the expensive three-run proofs happen ONCE at merge time, owned by the lead. that removes ~10 box-hours of duplicate benching from the queue.

Scott: MEETING PREP t-20261012-ef72 — scott
POSITION: The reader is the whole game, and today showed the fastest lane: segmentation-side rescue is worth 23 easy items in one PR (barry 28 to 51, zero losses, item-verified by me), while classifier swaps are worth 0 to +10 and do not replicate across seeds (S10b: canonical +10, held-out 0). Measured ceilings on the current head: the letter-digit twin class fully explains just 5 easy + 3 hard items; 28 of 49 failing easy items carry substitutions as their ONLY error kind; top easy substitutions are a->u 5, t->R 4, l->I 4. Spend compute on the floor route and size every lever before building it. Second cost driver: verification churn on moving heads.
PROPOSAL 1: HELD-OUT FIRST, standing rule: screen on seed 1, then exactly one held-out seed-2 run BEFORE any three-run proof. Worth: a void round plus a full proof round cost ~1.5h of the box; the seed-2 check that killed the candidate took four minutes.
PROPOSAL 2: REVIEWS BIND TO A SHA: an approving review names the head sha it covered; any push after that re-opens verification for the DELTA only, and authors announce pushes to a PR under review. Worth: marcus verified wave 3 (44/13), head was wave 5 (51/12) - the delta hid a hard regression (snow-0001) that a sha-bound record would have surfaced without a second full review.
PROPOSAL 3: POOLED SEEDS AS THE HEADLINE: n=100 makes one item one percent; exact-match deltas of +1 to +5 flip between seeds (S10b: +10 pooled, p=0.076). Make two-seed pooled n=200 the headline and per-seed runs the labeled screens. Worth: decisions stop pricing noise as progress; costs one extra suite run per claim.

Barry: MEETING PREP t-20261012-ef72 — barry
POSITION: Speed and quality are the same lever on this floor: every unmeasured guess is expensive (a bench cycle is 7-13 min) and every measured cheap rule is now at diminishing returns. The 98/95 bar needs glyph-level fidelity work, bench-cycle economy, and coordination so two branches never fight over the same pixel. Evidence base today: easy 28 -> 54 measured in six waves, every wave evidence-first with controls, every dead end disclosed in the same message as the win.
PROPOSAL 1: BENCH-CYCLE ECONOMY (speed; worth 3-5x more selection loops per hour): adopt the cache+probe pattern lane-wide (lru-cached template nominals, height-ordered scans with short-circuit, probe matcher inside decision loops). Measured on my branch: 23s -> 1.13s median official read. Change = one tools/profiler recipe + the two patterns documented.
PROPOSAL 2: FINISH THE EASY LADDER FIRST (quality; worth the demo suite + visible bar): S8 PR #27 is five measured waves up (28 > 34 > 40 > 44 > 47 > 51, hard-neutral, tests green) and wave 6 (+3, band-gated thin otsu) is on deck. Merge #27, then one more matcher wave. Change = the merge + one wave.
PROPOSAL 3: TIE-RESOLUTION AS SHARED POLICY (quality+speed; worth killing the largest measured error class once): S15 ledger says 73-90% of wrong glyphs are near-ties; my anatomy says literal 1.0-vs-1.0 ties exist which scoring cannot break. ONE adjudication contract: context rules first, CNN vote only where it measured to separate (scott: his net on #27 head measures NEGATIVE, 47/12 ON vs 51/12 OFF - so the contract names who may vote where). Change = the contract.
